# Glossary {#sec-glossary}

Terms are defined here once and used consistently throughout. Add new terms in the same change that first uses them.

AIS
: Automatic Identification System — VHF-based exchange of vessel and navigational information [@itu-m1371].

Alias
: An identifier a transport gives a Thing in place of its IRI, such as an AIS station and linkage identifier.
  An alias may be temporary, and one Thing may have several (@sec-ais-identity).

ASM
: Application-specific message — application data carried in AIS binary messages [@imo-sn1-circ289].

AtoN
: Aid to navigation.

Authority
: A participant that issues notices under its own responsibility, such as a maritime administration or a wildlife management agency.
  Anyone can issue a notice; whether a receiver acts on it depends on its trust in the issuer (@sec-vocab-notices).

Binding
: The definition of how the semantic model is carried in one representation, and over each transport that carries it (Part III).

Cached representation
: A copy of a Thing held by anyone but its origin, changed only with changes from the origin (@sec-origins).

Change
: The creation, update or deletion of a Thing (@sec-changes).
  Withdrawing a Thing is an update, and its expiry a scheduled update.

Change notification
: A message telling a participant that a Thing has changed: the kind of change and a link to the Thing, with optional hints (@sec-change-notifications).

Class A
: A shipborne AIS station that meets the IMO carriage requirement for AIS [@itu-m1371].

Class B
: A shipborne AIS station not necessarily meeting the IMO carriage requirement, which transmits a restricted set of messages.
  A Class B CS station accesses the channel by carrier sense, a Class B SO station by self-organized time division [@itu-m1371].

CoAP
: Constrained Application Protocol — a web transfer protocol for constrained devices and networks, carried over UDP [@rfc7252].

Content key
: A single-use key that a sealed part is encrypted with, held in a Thing of its own and given to each receiver encrypted to that receiver's public key (@sec-sealed).

Contractual relationship
: A relationship that binds both of the Things it relates, such as a charter, and holds only when the owners of both have signed it (@sec-relationships).

Data Integrity
: The W3C specification for embedding a signature, as a proof, in a linked data document, made over the document's canonical RDF [@vc-data-integrity]; the form of persistent signatures (@sec-trust-security).

Data owner
: An organization or person that originates a Thing or is responsible for it, and signs it with a persistent signature.

Designation
: A relationship in which one party names another as authoritative for a kind of information in an area; the way authority is conferred (@sec-provenance).

Distrust statement
: A Thing in which a party says that a receiver should not rely on other Things, some of their versions, or what a source made over a period; the owner's own is its revocation (@sec-distrust).

DNSSEC
: The DNS Security Extensions, which sign DNS records, including signed proof that a name does not exist [@rfc4033].

Envelope
: What the framework itself reads to handle a Thing, which is never sealed: its IRI and type, its version and the versions it succeeds, its validity and scheduled changes, its usage terms and its proofs; the rest of the Thing is its content (@sec-sealed).

Event
: In Darwin Core, something that happens at a place during a period of time, such as a sighting.
  An event can contain several occurrences (@sec-vocab-observations).

Fidelity
: How completely a binding can represent a Thing.

Gateway
: An on-board component connecting a vessel's own networks to the framework.

GeoJSON
: A JSON format for geographic features [@rfc7946].

HTTPS resource record
: A DNS record describing how to connect to an HTTP service, including which HTTP versions it supports [@rfc9460].

IEC 61162-450
: Carriage of sentences over Ethernet.

IMO
: International Maritime Organization — the United Nations agency responsible for the safety of shipping [@imo-ais].

Intermediary
: A participant that derives Things from information its sources report, publishes them to receivers attributed to itself, and shows their sources only to those with a need to know (@sec-intermediaries).

IRI
: Internationalized Resource Identifier [@rfc3987] — the form of every Thing's identifier.

JSON-FG
: OGC Features and Geometries JSON — an extension of GeoJSON [@ogc-json-fg].

JSON-LD
: A JSON-based format for linked data [@json-ld11]; the basic representation of Things in the JSON-LD binding.

Link relation
: The type of a link from one resource to another, such as `monitor` [@rfc8288].

Management area
: An area in which official rules apply to vessels, such as limits on speed; a Thing of its own, to which notices refer (@sec-management-areas).

MCP
: Maritime Connectivity Platform — a framework for maritime digital services, including identity registries that issue certificates to maritime organizations, vessels, devices and services [@iala-g1183].

MMSI
: Maritime Mobile Service Identity — the number that identifies a station in the maritime mobile service, such as an AIS station [@itu-m585]; over AIS, an alias of the vessel or other Thing that the station belongs to (@sec-ais-vessels).

MQTT
: A publish/subscribe messaging protocol in which clients exchange messages on topics through a broker [@mqtt5].

MRN
: Maritime Resource Name — a URN namespace (`urn:mrn:`) for identifying maritime resources [@iala-r1023].

NAME
: The identifier with which an NMEA 2000 device claims its source address; on board, an alias of the device, which can change (@sec-binding-pgns).

Namespace
: The part of an identifier controlled by one naming authority, within which that authority defines terms or identifies Things.

Notice
: A Thing produced by an authority about an area or about other Things, such as a management zone or an exclusion zone around a whale (@sec-vocab-notices).

Occurrence
: In Darwin Core, organisms of one kind and state present at a place and time; itself a kind of event (@sec-vocab-observations).

OneNet
: NMEA's standard for on-board networks over IP; link-local, carrying PGNs.

Organism
: In Darwin Core, a particular organism or a group recorded as one, such as a pod of orca; a Thing with its own identity, observed in sightings (@sec-sightings-organisms).

Origin
: The server, or servers, that hold a Thing for its owner and alone apply changes to it; a split origin, such as a vessel and its shadow, merges any branches of a Thing's versions across its servers (@sec-origins).

OSCORE
: Object Security for Constrained RESTful Environments — protection of CoAP messages end to end [@rfc8613].

PATON
: Private AtoN.

Persistent signature
: A signature attached to a Thing that stays with it when it is stored, relayed or re-published; a Data Integrity proof over one version of the Thing (@sec-trust-security).

PGN
: Parameter Group Number — identifies a message type on NMEA 2000 and OneNet.

Private AtoN (PATON)
: An aid to navigation operated by a body other than the national authority responsible for aids to navigation.
  In the United States, any aid to navigation not maintained by the U.S. Coast Guard [@uscg-paton].

Provenance
: The record of who originated a piece of information and who relayed or transformed it: the Thing's own, stated and signed by its owner, and each copy's, recorded by the participant that holds it (@sec-provenance).

Relationship
: A link from one Thing to another, of a stated type: a property of the Thing it is from, or a Thing of its own when it has an owner, a period or a signature of its own (@sec-relationships).

Representation
: A family of messages or formats onto which a binding maps semantic concepts, such as sentences or PGNs.

Responsible party
: A person, organization or vessel to which a device's identity rolls up, in a given role, such as owner, charterer or master (@sec-responsible-parties).

Scheduled change
: A change given in advance with the time at which it takes effect, applied then if the Thing is still at the version it was scheduled against, such as a notice's expiry (@sec-changes).

Sealed part
: A part of a Thing encrypted within it, covered by its signature in that form, and readable only by those given its key (@sec-sealed).

Selective disclosure
: Revealing only some of the statements in a signed Thing, with a signature that still verifies them (@sec-sealed).

Semantic model
: The framework's common definition of what information means (@sec-semantic-model).

Sentence
: A text message defined by NMEA 0183 (IEC 61162-1).

Server-sent events
: A one-way stream of events from a server to a client over HTTP [@whatwg-html].

Shadow
: A shore-side representative of a vessel, holding its state and acting for it while it is out of reach.

Shore station
: An AIS station on land, operated by the national authority responsible for aids to navigation or, under a private AtoN identifier, by another body.

Sighting
: An observation of one or more organisms at a place and time: a Darwin Core occurrence, or an event containing occurrences (@sec-sightings-organisms).

SOLAS
: The International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea, whose Chapter V requires many ships to carry AIS [@imo-ais].

Talker identifier
: The part of an NMEA 0183 sentence that identifies its source; together with the port it arrived on, an alias of the source (@sec-binding-sentences).

Thing
: Anything the framework describes, tangible or intangible — including relationships and schemas.

Transparency log
: A public, append-only log of certificates or signatures, which anyone can audit.

Transport
: A network or link that carries a binding's representation, for example NMEA 2000 or OneNet.

Usage terms
: What a holder may do with a copy of a Thing, stated by its owner as a license, possibly an ODRL policy; distinct from who may access the Thing (@sec-rights).

Validity
: How long a value holds in the world, expressed as a scheduled update that marks it as no longer current; distinct from how long a cached representation may be used (@sec-validity).

VDES
: VHF Data Exchange System.

Version
: The state of a Thing from one change until the next, identified by an IRI of its own, distinct from the Thing's (@sec-versions).

Vocabulary
: A module of classes and properties for one domain (Part II).

WebPKI
: The public key infrastructure of certificate authorities whose root certificates are trusted by web browsers' root programs.

WebSocket
: A protocol for two-way communication between a client and a server over one connection [@rfc6455].

Zero trust architecture
: An architecture in which no device is trusted because of where it is on the network, and each request is authenticated and authorized [@nist-sp800-207].
